correctness.rationale: A complete symbolic case analysis proves the if-and-only-if manipulation criterion under common priority. An exact exhaustive checker independently evaluates both the round-based and rank-scan implementations on all \(216\) three-student profiles and every false report, checks the \(2	imes2\) safe boundary, and recovers exactly \(36\) bad profiles, \(36\) vulnerable student-profile pairs, \(72\) profitable reports, and six school-relabeling classes.

value.rationale: The Boston mechanism is a canonical school-choice rule whose manipulability motivated major policy reforms. A common priority is a natural and widely studied special case. The result completely resolves the first balanced square market where strategic failure appears, providing a necessary-and-sufficient profile criterion, exact incidences, vulnerable-priority-rank structure, profitable-report multiplicity, and a compact symmetry classification.
